Reject the obvious tool and give the cost

main_argument_chains.claim: An agent model with a wage floor of $70,000, mandatory two-year college and one innovator in ten maximizes income and schooling metrics, while leave lengths can be set for happiness because they do not move output.
support_steps: Simulate each citizen's schooling, search and pay from labor-statistics shares
Deflate wages with a two-cycle inflation anchored to a stable country
Score income, schooling and gender with three cheap metrics
Sweep the floor and take the peak of the income metric
Rerun with randomized emergency populations and report linear scaling
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Adopt the floor, the 10-and-3-month leave and the young, balanced founding mix, and treat infrastructure as the binding limit on evacuation.

warnings.warning: The interpolation weights are printed on one line without the divisor. The recorded form divides by the distance between the 10th and 25th percentiles.
The birth probability is broken over several lines, with the peak term and the children divisor separated. The reconstructed form peaks at age 26 and scales as 1/(b+1).
The investment expression is garbled, with the welfare term misplaced. The recorded form follows the prose statement that a zero-income consumer is in debt by the welfare amount.
The equality metric prints the squared share gap across two lines and detaches the weights. The sum of women times squared gap, normalized by the labor force, matches the prose.
The inflation formula is printed with the fraction detached from the sine. The recorded two-sinusoid form matches the surrounding description of a 20-year cycle plus an annual wiggle.
